messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed Buchwald-Hartwig amination of 1-bromo-4-(trifluoromethyl)benzene with 4-methylaniline; choose the ligand, base and isoxazole additive.

picks.reason: L2/B1 is the strongest established ligand–base combination, so testing a new additive directly probes its potential.
This screens another untested additive under the leading conditions without changing multiple variables.
A6 is untested with the best-performing ligand and base, making it a useful focused additive screen.
Testing the top additive with B2 isolates whether its poor result with A20 was due to the base or additive.
Pairing the best additive with B3 provides a direct comparison to the leading B1 condition and the prior B3 result.
